context: R-linear subgroup of a module stable under scalar multiplication
editorial_screening_reason: The ProofWiki source requires a module structure on the subset inherited from M, along with closure under the scalar operation. In standard algebra these requirements are equivalent to being an additive subgroup stable under all scalar multiplication. The definition does not say that any arbitrary subset of M is automatically a submodule and must not be merged with an ideal of a ring, even though ideals are special submodules of R.

formulations.text: For a left R-module M, a subset N⊆M is a submodule when N is an additive subgroup of M and rn∈N for every r∈R and n∈N, with the addition and scalar multiplication restricted from M.

context: Topology P(S) on a nonempty set S (source scope)
editorial_screening_reason: ProofWiki's direct definition explicitly assumes S is nonempty and defines the discrete topology as its entire power set. The same construction also makes sense for the empty set, but that extension has not been separately cited in this batch. The nonempty version is sufficient to define the two-point discrete target in the connectedness characterization. Do not confuse a discrete topological space with a discrete category.

formulations.text: For a nonempty set S, the discrete topology is τ=P(S), the family of every subset of S; thus every subset is open in the resulting topological space (S,τ).
